brief: A three-storey cabinet with at least three drawers.

requirements.evidence: A vertical tower of three full hex bases at cell (0,0) on levels 0, 1 and 2 (piece:0,0,0, piece:0,0,1, piece:0,0,2), joined by snaps and capped. Final check_build: ok, no issues, meshClash clear.
Three drawers, all on level 0: drawer:0#-1,0#cut (on half-s at -1,0,0), drawer:0#0,1#cut (on half-n at 0,1,0) and drawer:0#1,0#cut (on half-n at 1,0,0). Each half base is locked with joint bolts.

requirements.requirement: Drawers spread across the three storeys
requirements.evidence: Every drawer is on storey 0. Half bases placed at level 1 over a full base were refused as UNSUPPORTED even after a cover, a snap and a joint bolt, so no drawers went on levels 1 or 2.

finish.summary: Built a three-storey tower (three stacked full hex bases at (0,0)) with three drawers on the ground storey, using half bases at (-1,0,0), (1,0,0) and (0,1,0). Joints are locked, open faces are capped, and check_build reports no issues with meshClash clear. The drawers are all on the bottom storey only; I could not place any on the upper storeys because half bases there were unsupported. The build is a compromise on that point. Nothing was checked for material, strength or load.

M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
